scope: Proposition 4.13 (Retarded stationary tests) of the manuscript “Quantitative Near-Kerr Evolution and Generic C2 Future Inextendibility” (preprints/Quantitative-Near-Kerr-Evolution-and-Generic-C2-Future-Inextendibility-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 264 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 cd38cc55e3c203a3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 38. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a compact test support and a finite number of required angular derivatives. There are a sufficiently high fixed test Sobolev order q∗ and a finite polynomial degree N∗ with the following property. Choose the filter order P sufficiently large and σ0 > 0 sufficiently small, then take Λ, R sufficiently large in the order specified below. For 0 < Re ζ ≤ D∗ on that strip and a compactly supported test f of order q∗, the spatial transpose equation MR(ζ)t v∗ = f has a solution satisfying ∥v∗∥Ḣ−4(K) ≤ CR3ι ⟨ζ⟩N∗ ∥f∥Hq∗ , (4.33) ∥(v∗, ry(∂ry + ζ)v∗)∥L2 ω ≤ Cr−1+ι y R3ι ⟨ζ⟩N∗ ∥f∥Hq∗ (ry ≫ 1). (4.34) Here K is any prescribed fixed compact reach, and the second bound includes the prescribed angular derivatives. The bounds are uniform down to Re ζ ↓ 0 on a fixed strip reaching a forward Laplace line. The slack ι > 0 can be arbitrarily small without making N∗ diverge. The associated tested operators are retarded.
